issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify that Animal.messageOnFeed() is an abstract method returning a String, and the template Farm.singFarmSongVerse() / feedAllAnimals() expect messageOnFeed() to produce a String to be printed. The solution repository instead defines Animal.messageOnFeed() to return a FeedResponse object (and subclasses return FeedResponse), introducing a return-type mismatch. This structural divergence will confuse students about the required signature and prevent straightforward implementation that matches the specification and template printing logic.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type of messageOnFeed() consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the solution to follow the specification: change Animal.messageOnFeed() and all subclass implementations (Seal, Pig, Goat) to return String (e.g., "Arf Arf!", "Oink!", "Maah!"), and remove or stop using FeedResponse; or (B) if FeedResponse is intentional, update the problem statement and template to declare/expect messageOnFeed() returning FeedResponse and adapt Farm.singFarmSongVerse() and feedAllAnimals() to extract the string (e.g., call .toString() or .getMessage()) when printing. Option A is recommended to match the UML and textual specification.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Animal.messageOnFeed() returns a String, and the template's singFarmSongVerse expects to print the animal's feed message as text. The solution repository, however, introduces a FeedResponse class and changes the abstract Animal.messageOnFeed() signature to return FeedResponse (and the Seal/Pig implementations return FeedResponse), while Goat erroneously overrides messageOnFeed() to return String. This creates an inconsistent API across artifacts: students are instructed to implement/consume messageOnFeed() as a String but the solution uses a different return type (FeedResponse) and inconsistent subclass overrides, causing mapping confusion and potential compilation/usage issues.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the API across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to match the problem/template by making Animal.messageOnFeed() return String (remove or make FeedResponse internal-only) and have all subclasses return String, or (B) update the problem statement and template to specify and use FeedResponse consistently (and adjust printing to use FeedResponse.getMessage()/toString()). Ensure all subclasses implement the same method signature to avoid compilation and conceptual mismatches.
